title: 考研英语二2013年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: In an essay entitled "Making It in America," the author Adam Davidson relates a joke from cotton country about just how much a modern textile mill has been automated: The average mill has only two employees today, "a man and a dog.
sentences.translation: 在一篇题为《在美国取得成功》的文章中,作者Adam Davidson讲述了一个来自棉花产区的笑话,说的是现代纺织厂的自动化程度有多高:如今一个普通工厂只有两名员工,"一个人和一条狗。人在那里是为了喂狗,而狗在那里是为了不让人靠近机器。"

sentences.text: The man is there to feed the dog, and the dog is there to keep the man away from the machines."
In the past, workers with average skills, doing an average job, could earn an average lifestyle.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2013-english-two/section2-part-a-1/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好their extra – their unique value contribution that makes them stand out in whatever is their field ofemployment.过去,拥有普通技能、做着普通工作的工人可以过上普通的生活。但如今,普通已经正式终结。仅仅普通已经不能让你获得过去那样的待遇。当如此多的雇主能够更广泛地接触到远超普通水平的廉价外国劳动力、廉价机器人、廉价软件、廉价自动化设备和廉价天才时,这已经不可能了。因此,每个人都需要找到自己的额外价值——使他们在各自就业领域脱颖而出的独特价值贡献。

sentences.text: But, today, average is officially over.
Being average just won't earn you what it used to.
It can't when so many more employers have so much more access to so much more above average cheap foreign labor, cheap robotics, cheap software, cheap automation and cheap geniuses.
Therefore, everyone needs to find

In a world where average is officially over, there are many things we need to do to support employment, but nothing would be more important than passing some kind of G. I. Bill for the 21st century that ensures that every American has access to post-high school education.
sentences.translation: 在一个普通已经正式终结的世界里,我们需要做很多事情来支持就业,但最重要的莫过于通过某种21世纪的《退伍军人权利法案》,确保每个美国人都能接受高中后教育。

sentences.text: A century ago, the immigrants from across the Atlantic included settlers and sojourners.
sentences.translation: 一个世纪前，来自大西洋彼岸的移民包括定居者和旅居者。在许多希望在美国永久定居的人当中，也有那些无意久留、赚些钱后就回国的人。1908年至1915年间，约有700万人抵达美国,而约有200万人离开。例如，大约四分之一的意大利移民最终永久返回了意大利。他们甚至有一个亲切的昵称——"uccelli dipassaggio",即过境之鸟。

sentences.text: Along with the many folks looking to make a permanent home in the United States came those who had no intention to stay, and who would make some money and then go home.
Between 1908 and 1915, about 7 million people arrived while about 2 million departed.
About a quarter of all Italian immigrants, for example, eventually returned to Italy for good.
They even had an affectionate nickname, "uccelli di passaggio," birds of passage.
Today, we are much more rigid about immigrants.
sentences.translation: 今天,我们对移民的态度要严格得多。我们将新来者分为两类：合法或非法,好或坏。我们把他们誉为未来的美国人,或把他们打上外来者的烙印予以驱逐。这种框架极大地导致了我们破碎的移民制度以及在如何修复这一问题上长期的政治僵局。我们不需要更多的分类,但我们需要改变思考分类的方式。我们需要超越合懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2013-english-two/section2-part-a-2/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好法与非法的严格定义。首先,我们可以认识到新的过境之鸟,那些生活并繁荣在灰色地带的人们。然后我们或许就能开始解决我们的移民挑战。

sentences.text: We divide newcomers into two categories: legal or illegal, good or bad.
We hail them as Americans in the making, or brand them as aliens to be kicked out.
That framework has contributed mightily to our broken immigration system and the long political paralysis over how to fix it.
We don't need more categories, but we need to change the way we think about categories.
We need to look beyond strict definitions of legal and illegal.
To start, we can recognize the new birds of passage, those living and thriving in the gray areas.
We might then begin to solve our immigration challenges.
Crop pickers, violinists, construction workers, entrepreneurs, engineers, home health-care aides and physicists are among today's birds of passage.
sentences.translation: 采摘工、小提琴手、建筑工人、企业家、工程师、家庭医疗护理人员和物理学家都属于当今的过境之鸟。他们是由工作、资金和思想流动驱动的全球经济中充满活力的参与者。他们更愿意随着机会的召唤来来去去。他们能够做到在一个地方工作而家庭在另一个地方。

sentences.text: They are energetic participants in a global economy driven by the flow of work, money and ideas.
They prefer to come and go as opportunity calls them.
They can manage to have a job in one place and a family in another.
With or without permission, they straddle laws, jurisdictions and identities with ease.
sentences.translation: 无论是否获得许可,他们都能轻松地跨越法律、管辖权和身份。我们需要他们把美国想象成一个可以暂时发挥生产力而无需承诺永久居留的地方。我们需要他们感到家可以既在这里又在那里,他们可以光荣地属于两个国家。

sentences.text: We need them to imagine the United States as a place where they can be productive for a while without committing themselves to staying forever.
We need them to feel that home can be both here and there and that they can belong to two nations honorably.
Accommodating this new world of people in motion will require new attitudes on both sides of the immigration battle.
sentences.translation: 适应这个人员流动的新世界将需要移民争论双方的新态度。超越对与错的文化战争逻辑意味着开辟中间地带,并理解管理当今的移民需要多种途径和多种结果,包括一些在现有制度下难以通过合法方式实现的结果。

sentences.text: Looking beyond the culture war logic of right or wrong means opening up the middle ground and understanding that managing immigration today requires multiple paths and multiple outcomes, including some that are not easy to accomplish legally in the existing system.

Scientists have found that although we are prone to snap overreactions, if we take a moment and think about how we are likely to react, we can reduce or even eliminate the negative effects of our quick, hard-wired responses.
sentences.translation: 科学家发现，尽管我们容易做出过激的本能反应，但如果我们花一点时间思考自己可能会如何反应，就能减少甚至消除这种快速的、与生俱来的反应所带来的负面影响。

sentences.text: Snap decisions can be important defense mechanisms; if we are judging whether someone is dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react very quickly, within milliseconds.
sentences.translation: 快速决策可能是重要的防御机制；如果我们在判断某人是否危险时，我们的大脑和身体会在几毫秒内做出非常迅速的本能反应。但我们需要更多时间来评估其他因素。研究表明，要准确判断某人是否善于社交，我们至少需要一分钟，最好是五分钟。判断性格中的复杂方面，如神经质或开放性，需要一段时间。

sentences.text: But we need more time to assess other factors.
To accurately tell whether someone is sociable, studies show, we need at least a minute, preferably five.
It takes a while to judge complex aspects of personality, like neuroticism or open-mindedness.
But snap decisions in reaction to rapid stimuli aren't exclusive to the interpersonal realm.
sentences.translation: 但对快速刺激做出的本能决策并不仅限于人际领域。多伦多大学的心理学家发现，仅仅看几毫秒的快餐标志就会促使我们的阅读速度提高百分之二十，尽管阅读与进食几乎没有关系。我们会无意识地将快餐与速懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2013-english-two/section2-part-a-3/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好度和不耐烦联系起来，并将这些冲动带入我们正在做的其他任何事情中。接触快餐闪现画面的受试者也倾向于认为一段音乐持续时间过长。

sentences.text: Psychologists at the University of Toronto found that viewing a fast-food logo for just a few milliseconds primes us to read 20 percent faster, even though reading has little to do with eating.

We unconsciously associate fast food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing, Subjects exposed to fast-food flashes also tend to think a musical piece lasts too long.
John Gottman, the marriage expert, explains that we quickly "thin slice" information reliably only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study.
sentences.translation: 婚姻专家John Gottman解释说，只有在我们将这种快速反应建立在"厚切片"式的长期研究基础上之后，我们才能可靠地快速"薄切片"信息。当Gottman博士真正想要评估一对夫妇是否会在一起时，他会邀请他们到他的岛屿静修所进行更长时间的评估：两天，而不是两秒钟。

sentences.text: When Dr. Gottman really wants to assess whether a couple will stay together, he invites them to his island retreat for a much longer evaluation: two days, not two seconds.
Our ability to mute our hard-wired reactions by pausing is what differentiates us from animals: dogs can think about the future only intermittently or for a few minutes.
sentences.translation: 我们通过暂停来抑制与生俱来的反应的能力，正是我们与动物的区别所在：狗只能间歇性地或在几分钟内思考未来。但从历史上看，我们每天大约有百分之十二的时间在思考长远问题。尽管技术可能会改变我们的反应方式，但它并没有改变我们的本性。我们仍然拥有超越诱惑、扭转高速趋势的想象力。

sentences.text: But historically we have spent about 12 percent of our days contemplating the longer term.
Although technology might change the way we react, it hasn't changed our nature.
We still have the imaginative capacity to rise above temptation and reverse the high-speed trend.
Europe is not a gender-equality heaven.
sentences.translation: 欧洲并非性别平等的天堂。尤其是,企业职场永远不会完全对家庭友好,除非女性成为高层管理决策的一部分,而欧洲顶级企业治理职位仍然绝大多数由男性担任。事实上,女性在欧洲企业董事会中仅占14%的席位。

sentences.text: In particular, the corporate workplace will never be completely family-friendly until women are part of senior management decisions, and Europe's top corporate-governance positions remain overwhelmingly male.
Indeed, women hold only 14 per cent of positions on European corporate boards.
"Personally, I don't like quotas," Reding said recently.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2013-english-two/section2-part-a-4/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好Reding, a result seen in France and other countries with legally binding provisions on placing women intop business positions.Reding最近说:"就个人而言,我不喜欢配额制。但我喜欢配额制所带来的结果。"配额制能促成行动:根据Reding的说法,它们"为平等开辟道路,并打破玻璃天花板",这一结果在法国和其他对女性担任企业高层职位有法律约束性规定的国家已经显现。
